name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs *after* every major design change, not before. This keeps the design loop fast and fluid while still catching accessibility failures early. The trade-off is that we accept occasional last-minute fixes when contrast slips through—but the speed and focus of iteration outweighs the risk.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A live checker after every change risks training us to ignore warnings until the last second—designers will treat it like a nagging pop-up, not a real guardrail. Better: a pre-submission gate that blocks only when contrast drops below WCAG AA, but lets trivial slips slide; that forces discipline without killing momentum. Settle it with a one-week trial: measure how often it blocks versus how many real failures it catches.
